description: We are a student-led team combining technical experience, curiosity, and problem-solving. With a background in cloud computing and technology alongside a strong interest in software development, we aim to use NASA Earth observation data to build practical, cloud-based solutions for wildfire monitoring and environmental analysis. Through collaboration and innovation, we seek to turn complex satellite data into accessible, meaningful insights.
summary:
Thermion is an interactive web platform designed to help users explore and understand wildfire activity using NASA Earth observation data. Our project addresses the challenge of making complex satellite information easier to access, visualize, and understand.

Using NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), Thermion presents wildfire and thermal anomaly data through a modern, user-friendly interface. Our goal is to turn scientific data into meaningful information that can be explored by students, researchers, and the general public without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

Wildfires threaten ecosystems, communities, and the environment worldwide. By making satellite-based fire information more accessible, Thermion helps raise awareness of wildfire activity and demonstrates how NASA's open data can support environmental monitoring and informed decision-making.

Thermion combines cloud data analysis, web development, and user-centered design to bridge the gap between complex Earth observation data and everyday users.
details:
THERMION — Project Details

THERMION is a bilingual web platform designed to make NASA's satellite thermal activity data easier to explore, analyze, and understand. Using NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), our platform transforms complex MODIS and VIIRS observations into interactive maps, visualizations, and meaningful insights.

How It Works

Users can select geographic regions, date ranges, and satellite sources to retrieve and explore thermal hotspot observations. THERMION offers four main features:

  • Interactive Fire Map: Visualizes satellite detections with detailed information about location, time, confidence, and thermal measurements.
  • Fire Activity Calendar: Designed to display historical activity patterns while distinguishing missing data from days with zero detections.
  • Regional Analysis: Organizes observations into geographic and time-based summaries to help identify patterns.
  • Satellite Comparison: Displays MODIS and VIIRS observations side by side using synchronized maps.

Users can also filter observations and export results in CSV or JSON formats.

Technology and Innovation

We developed THERMION using TypeScript, Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre, and Recharts, integrating NASA FIRMS APIs for satellite observations. The website is hosted on Vercel.

Our main innovation is combining multiple analysis tools into one accessible platform while preserving important scientific differences between satellite instruments. Unlike simply displaying hotspot locations, THERMION provides structured comparisons, regional summaries, and transparent handling of missing data.

Impact and Design

THERMION aims to support students, researchers, environmental organizations, and the public by making Earth observation data easier to interpret. We prioritized a clean interface, responsive design, performance, and bilingual English-Arabic accessibility.

By connecting NASA's open data with user-friendly technology, THERMION demonstrates how satellite observations can improve environmental awareness and support informed decision-making.
